claims.text: A lattice-distortion-corrected MLIP combined with CALPHAD can accurately predict melting temperatures and entropies of fusion for multicomponent HEAs.
Atomic-size mismatch produces energy-landscape roughness that governs melting behavior in HEAs.
Standard harmonic approximations fail in high-entropy regimes because they do not represent severe lattice distortion and associated anharmonicity.
Nb-Ta-Ti-V is an example of a refractory HEA that can exist as a single BCC solid solution.
The target refractory HEAs have significant atomic-size mismatch and severe local lattice distortion.
CALPHAD can be used to identify stable single-phase compositions before MLIP-based simulation.
Training an MLIP on first-principles configurations containing local lattice distortions will represent the rough energy landscape relevant to melting.
MLIP molecular dynamics can be used with a Lindemann criterion to calculate melting temperature and entropy of fusion.
Anharmonic vibrations dominate the relevant behavior above 1500 K.
NbTaTiV has a Zener anisotropy ratio near unity and is approximately elastically isotropic at room temperature.
Local lattice distortion and chemical disparity flatten the potential-energy surface.
The rough energy landscape alters defect mobility and dislocation-core structures in HEAs.
Changes in defect mobility and dislocation structure shift thermodynamic stability limits and melting behavior.
Standard harmonic calculations and simple mixing rules assume an insufficiently smooth or simplified potential-energy landscape.
MLIPs trained on distorted configurations capture anharmonic entropy contributions and local-environment-dependent barriers to melting.
Machine-learning models trained on ordered compounds can predict HEA elastic moduli when lattice distortion is accounted for.
The proposed method will predict refractory-HEA melting temperatures within ±50 K of experiment where standard CALPHAD or harmonic methods err by more than 100 K.
The method will correctly predict entropy of fusion by capturing excess configurational and vibrational entropy from the distorted lattice.
The method is valid for single-phase BCC or FCC solid solutions when severe lattice distortion is the dominant feature.
W-Ta-V-Cr is a rapidly phase-separating system for which the method may incorrectly predict a stable single-phase melting point.
